questions.key_step: Power-reduction then cos20+cos100=cos40 (or cosine rule in sine form).
questions.justification: One familiar transformation chain on a classic textbook expression; no decision beyond the standard identities. Sits with 2024-P2-Q3-type single-trick questions at L1.
Factor plus sign analysis over [0,4pi] with interval bookkeeping; routine multi-step, no real insight. Below 2024-P1-Q3 (L3).

questions.key_step: Expand cos3t, sin3t (or cube power reduction to cos^3 2t).
questions.justification: Chain of routine identities (cubes, sum/difference of sixth powers) with arithmetic; the slick cos^3 2t identity is not needed. Routine chain = L2.
Pure algebraic expansion of a well-known identity; options can be checked at a special angle. JEE Main level.
Direct use of half-angle formulas on two expressions; one familiar move.
Telescoping product via triple angle - same idea as 2026-P1-Q12 (L4) but single-correct with options, a standard identity and only four factors; one level of insight lower.
Convert to one variable and take range of a quadratic on an interval; a single familiar method.
Two routine stages (exponential quadratic, then values in (-pi/2,pi/2) and tan 15 deg arithmetic). Routine chain = L2.

questions.key_step: AM-GM on sin^4 a, 4cos^4 b, 1, 1 with equality.
questions.justification: The equality-case AM-GM (or sum of squares) idea is not the first thing students try in a trig equation; after it the rest is short. Two ideas linked = L3.
Single well-known bounding trick, then listing multiples of pi.

questions.key_step: Polynomial in sin^2 t factors as t(t-1)(2t-1).
questions.justification: Reduction to a cubic in sin^2 and careful counting on a closed interval (endpoint 2pi); routine but several steps.

questions.key_step: tan(a+b) from sum and product of roots.
questions.justification: Standard combination of Vieta with the tan addition formula; algebra simplifies to lambda/sqrt2. Routine multi-step.

questions.key_step: Multiply by sin A, double repeatedly.
questions.justification: The classic doubling product with A = pi/33 = pi/(2^5+1); one familiar trick.
Log change of base, recognising a perfect square, then a quadratic in sin x with sign check; routine chain across two chapters.

questions.key_step: Expression <= 3/2 with equality only at x=y=pi/3.
questions.justification: Needs the extremal argument (inequality or discriminant) to force the equality case - two ideas linked; familiar to students who know cosA+cosB+cosC <= 3/2.

questions.key_step: tan t1 + tan t2 = BE/AB with tan t1 tan t2 = 1.
questions.justification: Figure decoding (equal sides of the rectangle), quadratic in tan, choosing the case from the ratio condition, then area and perimeter - several stages, integer answer with no options.

questions.key_step: tan A = tan(-B) gives sin t + cos t = n, n in {-1,0,1}.
questions.justification: General solution plus range restriction, domain check of tan and summing over six solutions; integer answer, slip risk in counting. Between 2023-P2-Q3 (L3) and 2026-P1-Q14 (L3).

questions.key_step: Simplify to tan a = 1/7, tan b = 1/3 then compound angle.
questions.justification: Direct half-angle simplification and tan(a+2b) arithmetic; one familiar move even in integer format.
